subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Unit 3 – Lesson 9: Writing – A short story
outcomes: I know the parts of a story plan: characters, place, problem and ending.
I can use direct speech, adverbs and time words in a story.
I can write a short story with the Past simple and Past continuous.

tf.s: In the model story, Ammar and Qais were at the stadium.
tf.why: The story happens at the stadium.

tf.s: Ammar fell down some steps and broke his foot.
tf.why: That is the problem in the story.
Amjed Rashid is the number nine, Ammar’s favourite player.

tf.s: At the end, Amjed Rashid gives Ammar two tickets for a match in April.
A story plan has four parts: characters, place, problem and ending.
tf.why: Planning these parts helps you write a good story.

tf.s: Direct speech goes inside quotation marks.

tf.why: They are adverbs; they tell us how someone does something.

tf.s: A good short story doesn’t need a problem.
tf.why: A problem makes the story interesting.

tf.s: “Suddenly” and “at last” are time words we can use in stories.
tf.why: Time words help the reader follow the events.

tf.s: Ammar broke his arm at the stadium.
tf.why: He broke his foot, not his arm.

boxes.why: He is the number nine, Ammar’s favourite player.

boxes.q: What did Amjed Rashid give Ammar?
boxes.why: He gave him two tickets for a match in April.
Direct speech shows the exact words in quotation marks.

boxes.q: Complete: I ___ (read) a book when the door opened.

boxes.why: Adverbs like happily describe the verb.

boxes.q: Which is a time word for stories?
boxes.why: Suddenly tells us something happened fast.

boxes.q: What is the first part of a story plan?
boxes.why: Who is in the story comes first in the plan.

boxes.q: Which month is the match in?
boxes.why: The tickets are for a match in April.
Use quotation marks, an apostrophe and a comma.

mcq.q: What was Ammar’s problem in the story?
o: He fell down some steps and broke his foot.
He was late for the match.
mcq.why: Falling and breaking his foot is the problem.

o: Amjed Rashid gives Ammar two tickets for a match in April.
mcq.why: The story has a happy ending.

mcq.q: Which list shows the parts of a story plan?
o: title, price, good points, bad points
mcq.why: These four parts make a story plan.

mcq.q: What do we put around direct speech?
mcq.why: Quotation marks show the exact words someone said.

mcq.q: Choose the best first sentence for a story.
o: Salim was walking along the beach when he saw a box.
Salim were walking along the beach.
mcq.why: It uses the Past continuous and Past simple to start the action.

mcq.q: Choose the correct line of direct speech.
o: What’s in the box he asked.
mcq.why: Quotation marks go around the words he said.

mcq.q: Which sentence uses an adverb well?
mcq.why: Happily describes how he said it.

mcq.q: Why does a good story need a problem?
o: It makes the story exciting and gives the characters something to solve.
It is the title of the story.

mcq.q: “My foot hurts!” What does this direct speech show the reader?
o: How Ammar feels after he falls
mcq.why: Direct speech shows the character’s feelings.

mcq.q: Why is the ending of Ammar’s story happy, even after his accident?
o: His favourite player gives him tickets for another match.
His foot was not really broken.
He won a prize at school.
He never went to the stadium.
mcq.why: Something good happens after the problem.
